children: was in the spotlight on Thursday as J.P. Morgan upgraded the neocloud firm to Overweight from Neutral, citing its “favorable” contracts that should boost revenue growth.

“We are upgrading CoreWeave to Overweight from Neutral, led by the favorable pricing backdrop for compute given the strong demand backdrop as well as the incremental willingness of the company to lean into short-term contracts at premium pricing, which drives our revenue and margin forecasts higher in contrast to a lackluster share price performance dictated by investor concerns around capital intensity,” analyst Samik Chatterjee wrote in a note to clients.
Chatterjee also upped his price target on CoreWeave to $125 from $120.

Delving deeper, Chatterjee said the stronger pricing backdrop is due to a “robust demand environment,” which has strengthened throughout the year. That's due to pricing changes in July for roughly 25% of its products; “frequent” price increases from CoreWeave's peers like Nebius

; pricing for short-term compute contracts from competitors that are almost three times the price of what CoreWeave has on longer-term contracts; and the company's ability to leverage this opportunity in various different ways.

“Relative to the favorable demand backdrop, CoreWeave also has expanded flexibility in addressing the capacity needs through shorter-term contracts relative to prior with the precedent offered by DDTL 5.5 closed in August, which in our view reflects the incremental confidence from lenders in relation to the sustainability of demand for GPUs,” Chatterjee explained. “We expect the company to more fully leverage the flexibility offered through improved acknowledgment of the demand backdrop in the debt markets to address capacity needs for shorter-term contracts, while also taking a more proactive approach with planned capacity to prioritize a higher mix of shorter-term contracts relative to recent years.”

title: CoreWeave in spotlight as JP Morgan upgrades, citing 'favorable' contracts
